sources.title: Nationally Determined Contribution 3.0 of the Republic of Moldova
sources.organization: Government of the Republic of Moldova; submitted to the UNFCCC
sources.temporal_coverage: Submitted 6 May 2025; subnational risk index cited is from 2023, with historical impacts and a non-time-specific rainfall outlook.
sources.methodology: Government NDC synthesizes climate, social-risk and adaptation evidence.
sources.limitations: Index does not name 28 districts or assess conflict.

sources.title: Opportunities and Challenges of Climate Adaptation Policies, Republic of Moldova
sources.temporal_coverage: Published February 2024; analysis based on information available through 28 November 2023 and disaster impacts over the preceding three decades.
sources.methodology: IMF analysis uses ND-GAIN indicators, disaster records and macroeconomic modelling.
sources.limitations: National and comparative estimates; modelled benefits are not observed project outcomes.

sources.title: Moldova: Drought Portal country profile
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.temporal_coverage: Undated profile; statistics and referenced plans cover different years, including drought records through 2022 and institutional sources from 2019-2024.
sources.methodology: FAO country profile compiles drought, livelihood, infrastructure and institutional indicators from listed sources.
sources.limitations: The page does not date the profile or establish that older plans and arrangements remain operational.

sources.title: Hydro-infrastructure rehabilitation to mitigate vulnerability to climate-driven extreme events in the Republic of Moldova
sources.temporal_coverage: Project listed as active for 2024-2027; accomplishments and budget delivery are reported through 2025, with later work ongoing or planned.
sources.methodology: UNDP project page describes design, pilot coverage, reported outputs and training.
sources.limitations: Project outputs and training do not establish reduced flood losses or durable watershed-wide resilience.

sources.title: Results of the Post-Disaster Needs Assessment Following the Dniester River Pollution Crisis Presented to the Public
sources.organization: National Crisis Management Centre, Government of the Republic of Moldova
sources.temporal_coverage: Government summary of the spring 2026 pollution crisis and the PDNA presented on 16 October 2026; full report was not yet posted on the page.
sources.methodology: Government summary of a PDNA conducted with UN, EU and World Bank methodology and sector teams.
sources.limitations: Only the official web summary was accessible; proposed recovery actions were still being finalized.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.58 (printed p.59), vulnerability and INFORM subnational-risk discussion.
claims.paraphrase: NDC cites a 2023 subnational index: administrative units face medium-to-very-high disaster/humanitarian risk; 28 of 34 districts have high or extreme child climate risk.
affected_groups: children in 28 high- or extreme-risk districts
institutions: Government of the Republic of Moldova
claims.limitations: Index is cited as a 2023 assessment; the NDC does not name the 28 districts.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.59 (printed p.60), territorial distribution of climate risks.
claims.paraphrase: NDC describes rainfall declining from north to south and expects about 100 mm more multiannual rainfall in uplands, with drought and potential flash-flood patterns.
claims.scenario: NDC outlook; the cited passage specifies no emissions pathway or forecast period.
institutions: Government of the Republic of Moldova
claims.limitations: The NDC gives territorial patterns, not named upland districts or localized probabilities.

claims.locator: PDF physical pp.59-60 (printed pp.60-61), rural women and climate impacts.
claims.paraphrase: Rural women spend 20-25 hours weekly on water and farm tasks; drought can raise workload 30%, while floods and erosion burden uninsured women farmers.
institutions: Government of the Republic of Moldova
claims.limitations: The cited figures are national NDC estimates and do not identify individual localities.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.60 (printed p.61), child poverty, protection risks and environmental impacts.
claims.paraphrase: Rural poor, Roma, migrant/refugee and disabled children are among the poorest.
institutions: Government of the Republic of Moldova
claims.limitations: Policy pathway, not district-level evidence of climate-caused protection incidents.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: NDC says environmental impacts heighten child-labour, early-marriage, abuse and neglect risks.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.5 (printed p.5), abstract and climate sensitivity/readiness discussion.
claims.paraphrase: IMF attributes Moldova's climate sensitivity to agriculture, rural livelihoods, energy imports and limited public resources; it identifies weaker disaster preparedness, farm adaptation and infrastructure.
claims.limitations: The IMF presents national comparative analysis rather than local hazard estimates.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.7 (printed p.7), disaster costs and affected population.
claims.paraphrase: IMF estimates past climate-disaster losses near 12% of 2019 GDP cumulatively and an average 3% of the population affected by disasters over three decades.
claims.limitations: These are aggregate historical estimates and do not describe distribution among districts or groups.

claims.locator: PDF physical pp.5 and 22 (printed pp.5 and 22), adaptation investment conclusions.
claims.paraphrase: IMF says adaptation investment can reduce disaster losses, but domestic financing is constrained by debt and growth risks, making external concessional support and reforms important.
institutions: Government of the Republic of Moldova
claims.limitations: Benefits are modelled; the paper does not evaluate a particular adaptation project.

claims.locator: FAO Moldova profile, historical-drought and environmental vulnerability sections.
claims.paraphrase: FAO describes the south as hot and arid, with 5-6 droughts per decade; about 75% of Moldova is dry, subhumid or semiarid land.
institutions: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
claims.limitations: The undated profile combines indicators with different reference years; the drought frequency is not a forecast.

claims.locator: FAO Moldova profile, social, economic and infrastructure vulnerability sections.
claims.paraphrase: FAO reports rural livelihoods depend heavily on agriculture, 90% of production is rain-fed, and poor backyard producers and small farms have limited credit or subsidy access.
geographies: North, Center, South and Gagauzia regions
institutions: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
claims.limitations: The page compiles indicators from different years and does not provide current district-level household estimates.

claims.locator: FAO Moldova profile, institutional vulnerability section; National Drought Plan and water-hazard arrangements.
claims.paraphrase: FAO lists a 2019 National Drought Plan, local emergency commissions' five-year preparedness plans and water-hazard warning and response protocols.
claims.limitations: FAO does not date its profile or verify that these older plans and protocols remain active or effective.

claims.locator: UNDP project overview and expected results; pilot-area and objective sections.
claims.paraphrase: An active 2024-2027 project covers five named watersheds and targets flood early warning, dam safety and local integrated water-resources governance.
claims.limitations: Project design and expected results do not establish that intended outcomes have been achieved.

claims.locator: UNDP project accomplishments, monitoring-network and equipment items.
claims.paraphrase: UNDP reports procurement of 10 hydrometeorological stations for five pilot areas and ground-penetrating radar for national dam monitoring.
claims.limitations: Procurement is reported; the page does not confirm that every station is operational or quantify warning performance.

claims.locator: UNDP accomplishments, local action groups in pilot sub-basins.
claims.paraphrase: Local action groups involve residents of eight districts, particularly women and vulnerable groups, in flood plans, dam priorities and protective measures.
claims.limitations: The project page reports group establishment and participation, not completed flood-loss reduction.

claims.locator: UNDP accomplishments, specialist training items for climate modelling and dam/water management.
claims.paraphrase: UNDP reports training 35 specialists in digital climate-event modelling, 60 in dam flood-safety, and 50 in water-structure operation and assessment.
claims.limitations: Training counts do not show retention, routine use or subsequent response performance.

claims.locator: Government PDNA summary, incident cause, Cosăuți water-abstraction suspension and affected-population estimates.
claims.paraphrase: After Russia attacked Ukraine's Novodnistrovsk hydro plant, Dniester oil pollution halted Cosăuți abstraction; 200,000 faced disruption risk and 100,000 temporarily lost centralized water.
claims.limitations: Full PDNA unavailable; summary attributes pollution to attack, not climate.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Government links attack to pollution and service disruption; no climate trigger is identified.

claims.locator: Government PDNA summary, vulnerable groups, Soroca District impacts and Bălți service adaptations.
claims.paraphrase: Older, disabled, low-income and transport-limited people faced added difficulty; Soroca was most affected and Bălți moved classes online.
claims.limitations: The summary identifies groups and locations but does not disaggregate impact counts among them.

claims.locator: Government PDNA summary, immediate response and continuity of essential services.
claims.paraphrase: Authorities, partners and businesses distributed over 620 tonnes of water; emergency medical services continued while some non-urgent care was rescheduled.
claims.limitations: The summary reports immediate response outputs, not post-crisis service recovery or longer-term outcomes.

claims.locator: Government PDNA summary, recovery needs and proposed priority action packages.
claims.paraphrase: Proposals include alternative water sources, safety plans, real-time monitoring, cross-border protocols with Ukraine, civil-protection training and support for vulnerable communities.
claims.limitations: Recommendations were provisional at presentation and were not evidence of implementation or tested capacity.

search_audit.query: Moldova southern region drought subnational climate vulnerability rural women districts FAO
search_audit.outcome: Read the official NDC's district-level risk summary, FAO's southern-region drought profile, IMF national vulnerability analysis and named UNDP watershed coverage.

search_audit.query: Moldova climate change conflict Transnistria refugees energy vulnerability report UNHCR government
search_audit.outcome: The NDC describes environmental exposure and child-protection risks among poor children, including Roma and migrant/refugee children; no local climate-to-armed-conflict estimate was found.

search_audit.query: Moldova armed attack infrastructure water service disruption conflict adaptation project response
search_audit.outcome: The government PDNA summary links an attack on a Ukrainian hydro plant to pollution and Moldovan water-service disruption; this is a reverse security-to-service pathway, not climate causation.

search_audit.query: Moldova local adaptation plans early warning stations watershed flood resilience community
search_audit.outcome: Read UNDP's active watershed project and reported station, local action-group and training outputs; older drought plans are clearly dated or treated as status-unverified.

gaps: MDA does not appear in EXISTING_COUNTRIES.json; no baseline source record was available to extend for this ISO.
The NDC and IMF paper do not establish a local climate-to-armed-conflict pathway; NDC child-protection risks are source-stated but are not conflict-incidence estimates.
The full October 2026 Dniester PDNA was not yet posted; incident and response claims rely on the Government's direct summary, and proposed recovery actions were provisional.
The World Bank water-security diagnostic timed out and the 2025 UNDP vulnerable-groups report exceeded the reader limit; neither report's search snippets were used as evidence.
The UNHCR 2025 annual report PDF returned an access/rate-limit error and was not used as evidence.
No directly read source showed armed insecurity interrupting delivery of a named climate-adaptation project in Moldova.
